name: Jaddua
title: Descendants of Yeshua in the Time of Nehemiah
summary: Jaddua (also known as Jaddai) was a descendant in the high priestly line after the return from exile in Babylon. He is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as the son of Eliashib and father of Jonathan (or Johanan). He is associated with the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls and temple service during the Persian period.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the High Priestly Lineage
keyEvents.description: Jaddua is mentioned as part of the high priestly genealogy in the book of Nehemiah, as the son of Eliashib and a link in the priestly succession.

keyEvents.title: Temple Service After the Exile
keyEvents.description: Jaddua served as a central priest in Jerusalem during the period following the return from Babylon, when temple worship was restored.

keyEvents.title: Connection to Sanballat
keyEvents.description: One of Jaddua's sons married the daughter of Sanballat the Horonite, which led Nehemiah to drive him away because of mixed marriage.

keyEvents.title: Registration of Priestly Heads
keyEvents.description: During Jehoiada's time, the priestly heads were registered in the genealogy of the Levites, which was important for preserving the integrity of the holy service.

keyEvents.title: Nehemiah's Reforms
keyEvents.description: Jehoiada lived during a period marked by Nehemiah's religious and social reforms, which included cleansing the priesthood and reinstating Sabbath observance.
